answer: A stake-backed reputation system resists sybils by making each identity expensive to build and worthless to copy. An agent must lock a deposit and earn attestations from independent peers through real work, so a newcomer starts with near-zero trust no matter how many clones it spawns. Like a willow that only roots where planted, trust must grow from sustained service, not claims. A crystal-clear ledger makes that history checkable, and a reef of small independent verifiers cross-checks it, so fakes face deposits, time, and failed audits while honest agents build non-transferable reputation.
